memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: initial assessment of COPD.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Mrs X reports dyspnoea on walking uphill and occasional wheeze for 6 months.
EXAMINATION: BP 138/84 mmHg, weight 68 kg, BMI 24.2 (overweight). Respiratory rate 20, SpO2 94% on room air, diffuse wheeze bilaterally.
IMPRESSION: COPD, moderate severity. Advised diet and activity due to BMI ≥23.
ARRANGEMENTS: Start tiotropium inhaler OD, salbutamol inhaler SOS, budesonide-formoterol 200/6 inhaler BD. Order fasting lipid profile, fasting blood sugar, spirometry, chest X-ray. Return if chest pain, breathlessness at rest, fever >39°C, or haemoptysis.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Tiotropium bromide 18 mcg inhalation OD
Salbutamol 100 mcg inhalation SOS
Budesonide-formoterol 200/6 mcg inhalation BD

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
Fasting lipid profile: Total cholesterol 210 mg/dL (<200 desirable), LDL 130 mg/dL (<100), HDL 48 mg/dL (>40), Triglycerides 160 mg/dL (<150).
Fasting blood sugar: 98 mg/dL (70-100 normal).

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Spirometry: FEV1 1.68 L (55% predicted), FVC 2.80 L (85% predicted), FEV1/FVC 0.60 (<0.70). Consistent with moderate obstructive defect.
Chest X-ray: Hyperinflated lungs, flattened diaphragms, no focal consolidation.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I feel tired after climbing two flights of stairs and need to use my salbutamol inhaler about twice a week.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Follow-up appointment booked for 2025-07-10 at 10:00 am with Dr Priya Natarajan.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: routine COPD follow-up.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports improved exertional tolerance, uses salbutamol SOS once weekly.
EXAMINATION: BP 136/82 mmHg, weight 67.5 kg, BMI 24.0 (overweight). SpO2 95% room air, mild wheeze at bases.
IMPRESSION: COPD stable. BMI ≥23, reinforce diet and activity.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue current inhalers. Add short course prednisolone 10 mg OD for 5 days due to mild exacerbation symptoms. Repeat fasting lipid profile and fasting blood sugar. Return if worsening dyspnoea, fever >38°C, or increased sputum purulence.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Prednisolone 10 mg OD for 5 days
Tiotropium bromide 18 mcg inhalation OD
Salbutamol 100 mcg inhalation SOS
Budesonide-formoterol 200/6 mcg inhalation BD

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
Fasting lipid profile: Total cholesterol 202 mg/dL, LDL 124 mg/dL, HDL 50 mg/dL, Triglycerides 148 mg/dL.
Fasting blood sugar: 95 mg/dL.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Refer to Pulmonology, Dr S. Rao, for consideration of long‑term oxygen therapy assessment and optimisation of inhaler technique.
Clinical details: COPD, FEV1 55% predicted, BMI 24, on tiotropium, salbutamol SOS, budesonide-formoterol BD.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Pulmonary review: Patient demonstrates good inhaler technique, SpO2 92% on room air, no immediate need for LTOT. Continue current regimen, advise pulmonary rehab. Review in 3 months.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: annual COPD review and influenza vaccination.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: No exacerbations since last visit, occasional wheeze on exertion.
EXAMINATION: BP 134/80 mmHg, weight 66 kg, BMI 23.9 (overweight). SpO2 96% room air.
IMPRESSION: COPD stable. BMI ≥23, advise diet and activity. Annual lipid and glucose checked.
ARRANGEMENTS: Influenza vaccine administered today 2026-04-10. Continue tiotropium OD, salbutamol SOS, budesonide-formoterol BD. Return if new chest pain, worsening dyspnoea, fever >39°C, or haemoptysis.
